Not every dog can do this, and not every trainer can or should. With the owners' permission, I used Bishop to help communicate a lesson to Ryder. Dogs naturally understand other dogs better than they understand us. The goal wasn't to make Ryder love every dog she sees-it was to teach her that she doesn't need to react to every dog she sees. Before training, a simple neighborhood walk was nearly impossible. Seeing another dog meant lunging, pulling, and trying to start conflict. Through obedience work and carefully controlled sessions with Bishop, Ryder learned a valuable lesson: not every dog is a threat, and not every situation requires a reaction. Also notice how Bishop's corrections increase in intensity throughout the video. He starts with the minimum amount of pressure necessary and only escalates when Ryder chooses not to listen. That's how dogs naturally communicate with one another. Will I tell these owners to take her to a dog park and expect her to be everyone's best friend? Absolutely not. But can we give her a better quality of life by helping her calmly walk past another dog across the street? Absolutely. Not every dog needs this type of training, but some dogs can benefit tremendously from it. Braised Chicken Legs with Rice, Potatoes & Veggies🍗 Ingredients * 1 package chicken drumsticks (6–7 pieces) * 1-2 tbsp olive oil * 1 tsp salt * 1 tsp black pepper * 2 tsp garlic powder * 2 tsp onion powder * 2 tsp paprika * ½ tsp cumin * 1 jalapeño, diced * ½ red onion, diced * 1 tbsp sun-dried tomato paste * 1 tbsp @Loisa sofrito * 5–6 garlic cloves, minced * 4 cups chicken stock * 1 (8 oz) can tomato sauce * Small potatoes, halved (about 10–12 baby potatoes) * 1 zucchini, diced * Cooked white rice, for serving (let me know if you guys want my rice recipe) Instructions: 1. Clean the chicken with vinegar, then pat completely dry with paper towels. 2. Season the chicken with the salt, pepper, garlic powder, onion powder, paprika, and cumin. Toss until evenly coated. 3. Heat the olive oil in a large Dutch oven or deep skillet over medium-high heat. 4. Brown the chicken for 2–3 minutes per side until golden. It doesn’t need to be cooked through. Remove and set aside. 5. In the same pot, add the diced jalapeño and red onion. Cook for about 5 minutes until softened. 6. Stir in the sun-dried tomato paste and cook for 30 seconds. 7. Add the Loisa Sofrito and minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant. 8. Pour in the chicken stock and tomato sauce, stirring to combine. Bring to a gentle boil. 9. Return the chicken to the pot. Reduce the heat to low, cover, and simmer for about 1 hour, or until the chicken is fall-apart tender and the sauce has reduced. 10. About 20 minutes before the chicken is done, add the halved potatoes and diced zucchini. Continue simmering until the potatoes are fork-tender and the zucchini is cooked. 11. Serve over fluffy white rice and spoon plenty of the sauce over the top. #chickenlegs #braised #onepotmeals #cookwithme

Extra Gooey Cinnamon Rolls (Bakery-Style & No-Knead) Dough * 1 tsp yeast * 2 tbsp sugar * 343 g milk (about 1½ cups) * 480 g flour (about 4 cups + 2 tbsp) * 1 tsp salt * 60 g softened butter (about 4 tbsp) Filling * 140 g softened butter (10 tbsp) * 140 g brown sugar (about ⅔ cup) * 3½ tbsp ground cinnamon Butter Vanilla Frosting * 85 g softened butter (6 tbsp) * 180 g powdered sugar (about 1½ cups) * 1 tbsp vanilla extract Instructions 1. In a bowl, mix the yeast, sugar, and milk. Add the flour and mix until combined. Add the salt and softened butter, then stretch and fold (or coil fold) until the butter is fully incorporated. 2. Cover and let the dough rise for about 2 hours, or until doubled in size. 3. Roll the dough into a large rectangle. Spread the softened butter evenly over the dough, then sprinkle with the brown sugar and cinnamon. 4. Cut the dough into 6 long strips, then roll each strip into a cinnamon roll. 5. Sprinkle a little of the cinnamon sugar mixture into the bottom of the pan, then place the rolls on top. 6. Cover and let them rest for 15 minutes. 7. Mix a little milk with 1 tbsp melted butter, then spoon about 2 tbsp of the mixture over each cinnamon roll. 8. Bake at 350°F (175°C) for 25–30 minutes, or until golden brown. 9. As soon as they come out of the oven, cover them with a clean kitchen towel until warm. Then spread the frosting on top. 👩‍🏫내가 원하는 **‘추구미’**에 도달하려면  ✔️메이크업뿐만 아니라  ✔️헤어, 스타일링, 분위기까지 전체적인 합을 맞춰야 함 ✅원하는 대상의 스타일링 분석, 카피-> 미감 자체를 따라잡기 ⬇️영상 핵심 내용만 체크해보기 1. 메이크업만으로는 부족해! 전체적인 스타일링이 핵심  ‘얼굴이 다했다’는 생각은 금물: 뷰티 영상을 볼 때 무작정 화장법만 따라 하기보다는, 그 사람이 풍기는 전체적인 분위기와 스타일링 조합을 파악하는 게 중요해.  추구미 = 메이크업 + 헤어 + 패션 + 분위기: 내가 원하는 추구미에 맞춰 여러 요소를 종합적으로 바꿔야 메이크업도 훨씬 빛을 발하고 분위기가 완성돼! 2. 예시로 보는 추구미 분석 & 스타일링 팁 ✨ 1) 화려하고 독보적인 공주님 스타일 (ex. 장원영)  추구미 방향: "나는 특별하고 화려해 보이고 싶다!"  스타일링 포인트: 조금 더 진하고 또렷한 메이크업, 공들인 헤어 스타일링, 다이어트와 자기관리. 화려한 패션스타일(남들이 시도하지 않는) 🌿 2) 수수하고 깨끗한 청순 스타일 (ex. 정채연)  추구미 방향: "오밀조밀하고 수수하면서도 청순한 느낌을 내고 싶다!"  스타일링 포인트:  피부: 미백 앰플이나 톤업 크림을 활용해 맑고 하얀 피부 바탕 가꾸기.  헤어: 자연 흑갈색 톤 & 레이어드 컷으로 결을 살린 긴 생머리 연출.  아이 & 브로우: 눈썹 탈색 대신 결만 살리고, 눈은 점막만 채운 뒤 마스카라로 깔끔하게!  립 & 치크: 볼터치와 립을 강조해서 생기 더하기.  패션: 핀터레스트에 ‘청순 코디’를 검색해 마음에 드는 스타일을 찾은 뒤, 쇼핑앱(에이블리 등)에서 비슷한 옷을 매치해 보기! 3. 핵심 포인트 💖  분위기와 미감은 스스로 만드는 것:  스타일링과 분위기, 미감은 돈으로 살 수 없는 나만의 영역.  나를 가꾸는 기쁨 느끼기: 무작정 똑같이 따라 하기보다 나만의 추구미를 찾고, 화장을 통해 내 얼굴의 장점을 살리면서 나를 더 사랑하고 예쁘게 가꿔보기 💭Ps. 그 추구미를 “추구하는 이유가 뭐야?” 이 질문에서 자신의 결핍된 욕구와 니즈를 찾을 수 있고 그걸 채워가면서 만족하는게 자기관리야 -유리멘탈이 겉으로는 더 쎈 이미지를 가진 이유이기도 하달까?  이게 나쁜게 아니라, 그렇게 상호보완 하는게 자연스러운 법칙이거든 나 자신을 사랑하며 가꾸는 메이크업과 스타일링 화장 잘하는 언니 메이뮤와 오래 천천히 함께해💚

PART 1/2 Meet Beau. A 6-year-old German Shepherd / Great Pyrenees mix with a serious bite history. Beau had bitten his owner multiple times, a family friend, and during his last vet visit, he attempted to bite both staff and the veterinarian. He was overwhelmed, unsafe, and heading down a path with very few options left. Thankfully, his owners didn’t give up. They reached out and committed to a 6-week behavior modification board & train. After 5 weeks of structured behavior work, obedience, and muzzle conditioning, we returned to the same veterinary clinic that Beau struggled in before training. This was a high-stakes moment. There were multiple bite attempts, but here’s the difference: everyone stayed calm, neutral, and communicative. That changed everything. Was it perfect? No. Was Beau safer, more manageable, and able to be treated for a painful bacterial infection in his paw? Yes. Handling a 100+ lb dog with bite history is no small task. Huge respect to my apprentice Kevin and Beau’s owner for staying consistent and showing up when it mattered most. When a dog has a bite history, should they be written off as “dangerous,” or does the responsibility fall on the owner to step up, provide structure, and do the hard work instead of giving up? #DogTraining #dogs #dogtrainer #dogsoftiktok #behaviormod
